author: spurgeon
title: The Treasury of David
edition: C. H. Spurgeon, The Treasury of David: containing an original exposition of the Book of Psalms (London: Passmore and Alabaster, 1869-85), Vols. I-IV and VI in the 1881 printing; archive.org scans "thetreasuryofdav01spuruoft", "thetreasuryofdav02spuruoft", "thetreasuryofdav03spuruoft", "treasuryofdavid04spuruoft" and "treasuryofdavid06spuruoft" (University of Toronto), djvu OCR text
notes: Only Spurgeon's own Exposition is taken, not the Explanatory Notes and Quaint Sayings he gathered from other writers. Volume V (Psalms 111-119) is not among the scans used, and Psalms 54, 60 and 123 are left out because their verse numbers could not be read; elsewhere a comment whose verse could not be placed is left out. Spurgeon prints the King James Version's verse numbers, which in a psalm with a title are one or two lower than the Hebrew numbers the Open Word Bible uses: each excerpt is set on the Open Word Bible's verse, found by the difference in the number of verses. Each excerpt is Spurgeon's comment on one verse ("10. ...") or on the group of verses he prints before it, up to about 350 words and cut at a sentence end. Misreadings are corrected in library/corrections/spurgeon.json only where the same scan prints the word correctly many times.
